questions.note: Stature and head read right: about 1805 px for about 1855 mm in the full view, so roughly 0.97 px/mm, and the head is about 220 px, so about 226 mm. But the sleeved upper arms are about 150 px (about 155 mm) wide and the forearm rings wider still, while the waist between carrier and belt is pinched. Limbs read inflated against a narrow trunk.

Stance, lean and the low-ready diagonal of the carbine follow the reference. The right shoulder slab widens the outline on the viewer's left. The right foot is turned out to near profile, past the reference's roughly 45 degrees, and the carbine hangs a little further from the chest than drawn.

Most items are present and roughly placed: gaiter, carrier, three mag pouches, radio with antenna, pauldrons, forearm guards, thigh rigs, knee pads. But the right knee pad faces outward with the turned-out leg, the right-hip belt pouch at the front is absent or moved to the rear, the pauldrons are flat planks, and the two boots are different builds.

Order of layers is right and nothing obviously cuts through. But a tall rear-hip pouch stands off the belt with a lid sticking out, the shoulder plates ride off the deltoids, the radio pouch hangs past the back panel's edge, and the rigid forearm ring spans the bent right elbow, where it would bind. The trousers cling to crotch and seat like tights.

The kit's bulk is in the wrong places. The arms are swollen tubes and the forearm guards are full cylinders, while the carrier reads as a thin flat slab without the PALS and pouch depth that give a loaded JPC its mass. The trousers are skin-tight at the seat yet stovepipe below the knee. The values are uniform, so the layered weight of the reference is lost.

The left hand cups the handguard with the thumb over the top: acceptable. The right hand reads as resting beside the lower receiver with loosely curled fingers and a straight high wrist; the pistol grip does not visibly sit in the palm. The stock floats by the upper arm rather than being pinned under it as drawn.

defects.what: The right boot's forefoot is a smooth seamless wedge shell, like an overshoe or a sneaker, with lacing only at the ankle collar, and it does not match the laced-to-the-toe left boot. A pair of boots must be mirror images.
defects.fix: Mirror the left boot: laced vamp with eyelets to the toe box, rand, toe cap and lugged sole, as on a Zephyr-class mid boot.

defects.what: The right leg is externally rotated about 70 degrees: the foot is in near profile and the knee pad faces outward. That is beyond a relaxed standing turnout (10 to 20 degrees, passive maximum about 45), and the pad no longer sits where the drawing's front-facing pad is.
defects.fix: Reduce hip external rotation to about 30 to 40 degrees so the patella and pad face mostly forward and the foot points out as in the reference.

defects.what: The right hand does not read as closed on the pistol grip. The fingers curl loosely beside the lower receiver, the wrist is straight and high, and the grip is not seen entering the palm, so the hand looks like it hovers.
defects.fix: Seat the grip in the palm web, with middle, ring and little fingers wrapped around its front strap, the thumb over the selector side and the index finger straight along the receiver above the trigger guard.

defects.what: The hair is a solid smooth cap with a hard cut-out hairline at the temples, and a few thin spikes stick straight up from the crown. Real short hair has a soft hairline that thins into the skin.
defects.fix: Short tapered cut with a feathered hairline, fade at the sides and no isolated quills.

defects.what: The trousers are moulded to the crotch and to the buttocks (back view seam line), like tights. Combat trousers have a gusseted crotch and a loose seat that bridges between the thighs.
defects.fix: Give the trousers ease at seat and crotch with a gusset bridging the legs, as on a G3-class trouser.

defects.what: A tall pouch at the rear right hip stands well off the belt and buttock, and its lid sticks out at an angle, so it reads as floating rather than hung on the belt's webbing.
defects.fix: Mount it flat on the belt's PALS with its back panel against the belt, lid closed.

defects.what: The forearm guards are full rigid cylinders, the right one about 140 mm across, and on the flexed right arm the upper ring runs across the elbow crease, where a rigid tube would bind into the biceps.
defects.fix: Make them half-shell plates strapped to the outer forearm that stop short of the elbow crease, so the elbow can fold.

defects.what: The wear on the knee pads, pauldrons and guards is an even tan speckle over the whole face, like overspray. Real wear concentrates on edges, corners and high points where the part rubs.
defects.fix: Drive wear from curvature, edges and contact areas, with clean recessed faces.

defects.what: Shirt, carrier, pouches, pauldrons and gloves all sit at one mid warm-brown value. The reference separates a near-black shirt, an olive carrier and blue-grey pauldrons, so the layers lose their read even allowing for the warm key.
defects.fix: Shirt and gloves near black, carrier and pouches an olive-coyote mid value, hard armour a cooler grey, matched relative to the frame.

defects.what: The shoulder armour is a flat plank standing off the deltoid at an angle, not a shell that follows the shoulder's curve.
defects.fix: Form the pauldron as a curved shell cupping the deltoid, hung from the carrier's shoulder strap with a small even stand-off.

defects.what: The sleeved upper arm and forearm read about 150 mm wide, swollen tubes far thicker than a lean man's arm plus a combat-shirt sleeve, out of proportion with the narrow trunk.
defects.fix: Slim the sleeve to the arm, about 110 to 120 mm across the biceps with the fabric, and let the armour pieces carry the bulk.

defects.what: The reference's pouch on the belt at the right front hip, above the thigh rig, is missing at that place.
defects.fix: Put the pouch on the war belt at the right front hip, as drawn.

defects.what: The flash hider is bright bare copper or brass. A real A2-type muzzle device is black phosphate or nitride steel.
defects.fix: Dark parkerized steel with worn edges.

defects.what: The buttstock is built from pencil-thin bars around a large triangle, too spindly for a polymer carbine stock.
defects.fix: Solid polymer stock body with webs about 8 to 12 mm thick around any cut-out.

defects.what: The trouser camouflage shows hard square pixel steps in its blotches.
defects.fix: Raise the texture resolution or filter the pattern mask.

defects.what: Two thin stiff rods hang straight down from the bottom of the right thigh mag pouch, like antennas. Pull tabs or bungee tails would be soft and short.
defects.fix: Short soft webbing tabs or bungee loops.

defects.what: Small diamond tabs and blocks sit on the left upper arm and elbow with no strap or mount, as if glued on.
defects.fix: Attach each piece to a strap or remove it.

defects.what: The radio pouch hangs past the side edge of the back panel instead of being mounted on the panel's or the cummerbund's webbing.
defects.fix: Mount it on the back panel's PALS at the soldier's left, inside its edge.

ranked: [D9] Everything is one warm mid-brown value: shirt, carrier, pauldrons and gloves merge, so the reference's black-olive-grey layering, which tells a viewer what each layer is, is lost.
[D11] The arms are swollen tubes about 150 mm thick against a pinched waist, so the figure reads like an action toy, not a lean soldier in a combat shirt.
The carrier is a thin flat slab with three shallow flat-topped boxes. A loaded plate carrier has visible plate thickness, PALS rows and mag tops, which give it weight on the chest.
[D4] The hair is a hard-edged cap with a few quills on the crown, and the face reads rounder, softer and younger than the reference's lean, weathered man.
[D1] The right boot is a lace-less wedge shell over the forefoot and does not match the properly laced left boot.
[D2] The right leg is turned out about 70 degrees, past comfortable hip rotation: the foot is in profile and the knee pad faces outward instead of forward.
[D3] The right hand does not visibly close on the pistol grip. The fingers curl loosely beside the receiver, so the hold reads posed rather than gripped.
The stock floats beside the right upper arm instead of being pinned under the arm against the chest as drawn, so the carbine is carried by the hands alone.
[D5] The trousers cling to the crotch and seat like tights, then flare into stovepipes below the knee, which no combat trouser does.
[D8] The wear is a uniform tan speckle across every armour face. Real scuffing lives on edges and high points.
[D10] The pauldrons are flat planks angled off the shoulder rather than shells following the deltoid.
[D7] The forearm guards are full rigid cylinders, and on the flexed right arm the ring crosses the elbow crease where it would bind.
[D6] The rear-hip pouch stands off the belt with its lid sticking out, so it looks unattached.
[D12] The belt pouch at the right front hip in the reference is missing at that place.
[D13] The flash hider is bare copper. Real muzzle devices are dark phosphate or nitride.
[D14] The stock is drawn in thin bars, too delicate for a polymer carbine stock.
The gloves are smooth rubbery mitts with no knuckle padding or palm reinforcement, so they read as generic gloves rather than M-Pact-class.
[D15] The trouser camouflage shows square pixel steps.
[D16] Two stiff rods hang from the bottom of the right thigh pouch like antennas.
[D17] Small tabs on the left upper arm and elbow have no strap or mount.
[D18] The radio pouch hangs past the edge of the back panel instead of sitting on its webbing.
